---

- Story 11 completed: ticket-status audit trail and `applyStatusTransition` helper exist in `backend/src/services/ticketStatus.service.ts` — this story extends the allowed-transitions table with the `"escalated"` value that Story 11 deliberately left out (see the comment at `backend/src/services/ticketStatus.service.ts` lines 25–28).

This story calls that helper — do **not** re-invent a notification path.

- Coordinate with **Story 13 (view full ticket history)**: if not yet built when this plan is executed, this story must **not** clear/reset any ticket fields on escalation (only append to `statusHistory` and set `escalatedTo`). Full "history travels with the escalation" is closed out by Story 13.

## Story Goal

Add the **manual** ticket-escalation path so a logged-in agent (or admin/subadmin with the right grant) can flip a ticket to `status: "escalated"` and set `escalatedTo: <senior agent or admin>` from the ticket-detail sidebar's "⚠ Escalate ticket" button (see `attachments/detail-escalate-button.png`). Escalation:

1. Notifies the target (in-app via `createTicketNotification({ type: "ticket_escalated" })`, plus oversight nudge to admins/permitted subadmins).
2. Visibly flags the ticket in staff list/dashboard views (the existing `"escalated"` status is already counted in `statusCounts` at `backend/src/routes/ticket.routes.ts:337` — surface it in the queue chips and detail badge).
3. Preserves the ticket's full data (customer, `assignedAgent`, `category`, `priority`, messages, `statusHistory`) — the escalation is an **append** (`statusHistory.push`) plus two field writes (`status`, `escalatedTo`), never a wipe.

**Not in scope:** SLA-breach detection or any auto-escalation trigger (Story 28, `sla-automation`). Deep audit trail beyond the existing `statusHistory` (Story 13). Assignee handoff (`assignedAgent` stays as-is; escalation is orthogonal to reassignment — Story 25 owns manual reassignment).

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** No route accepts an "escalate" verb. `PATCH /tickets/:id/status` explicitly rejects `"escalated"` via `ALLOWED_MANUAL_STATUSES` (`backend/src/validation/ticket.schema.ts:88`). `Ticket.escalatedTo` is defined but never written. The `"ticket_escalated"` notification type exists (`backend/src/models/Notification.ts:30`) but is never emitted. `ticket.routes.ts` has a `TODO(Story 12 — escalate a ticket)` at lines 492–495 pointing at this gap.
- **New behaviour:** A new endpoint (`POST /tickets/:id/escalate`) — gated by the new `"tickets:escalate"` permission — sets `status: "escalated"`, `escalatedTo`, appends to `statusHistory`, emits `"ticket_escalated"` to the target, and `"ticket_needs_assignment"`-style oversight nudge to admins/permitted subadmins. Staff-facing list/detail surfaces render an "Escalated" flag (badge in row, badge + "Escalated to <name>" line in detail sidebar). Once escalated, transitioning back to `"in_progress"` (target picks it up) or `"closed"` remains available through the existing `PATCH /:id/status` because the allowed-transition table now includes those exits.

## Backend Tasks

### 1 — Extract an `escalateTicket` service function

**Create file:** `backend/src/services/ticketEscalation.service.ts`

Export a single function so Story 28 can call it directly (not via HTTP) when SLA breaches auto-escalate:

```ts
import { Types } from "mongoose";
import { Ticket, ITicket } from "../models/Ticket";
import { User } from "../models/User";
import { applyStatusTransition } from "./ticketStatus.service";
import { createTicketNotification, notifyTicketOversight } from "./notification.service";

export type EscalationReason = "manual" | "sla_breach";

export class InvalidEscalationTargetError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string) { super(message); this.name = "InvalidEscalationTargetError"; }
}

export interface EscalateTicketInput {
  ticket: ITicket;
  escalatedToUserId: Types.ObjectId;
  changedBy: Types.ObjectId;
  reason: EscalationReason;
}

export async function escalateTicket(input: EscalateTicketInput): Promise<ITicket> { /* … */ }
```

Behaviour:
- Validate the target: `User.findById(escalatedToUserId)` — must exist, `isActive: true`, `isDeleted !== true`, `role` in `["agent", "admin", "subadmin"]` (never `"customer"`). Throw `InvalidEscalationTargetError` on any failure.
- Reject self-escalation: `escalatedToUserId.equals(changedBy)` → throw `InvalidEscalationTargetError`.
- Set `ticket.escalatedTo = escalatedToUserId` **before** calling `applyStatusTransition`, so the audit `statusHistory` push and the field write commit together in one `ticket.save()` (the helper at `backend/src/services/ticketStatus.service.ts:73` saves).
- Call `applyStatusTransition({ ticket, nextStatus: "escalated", changedBy, reason: reason === "sla_breach" ? "auto_escalation" : "manual" })` — the `"auto_escalation"` reason is already declared at `backend/src/services/ticketStatus.service.ts:9`.
- Fire-and-forget notifications (best effort, do not await-fail):
  - `createTicketNotification({ recipient: escalatedToUserId, type: "ticket_escalated", ticketId: ticket._id })`
  - `notifyTicketOversight({ type: "ticket_escalated", ticketId: ticket._id })` — so admins/subadmins with `tickets:view_all` see the event even when they aren't the target.
- Return the mutated ticket.

**Do not** clear or reset `assignedAgent`, `priority`, `category`, `customer`, or `messages` — escalation is additive.

```ts
export const escalateTicketBodySchema = z.object({
  escalatedTo: z
    .string()
    .refine((v) => Types.ObjectId.isValid(v), { message: "escalatedTo must be a valid user id" }),
});
```

### 5 — Add `POST /tickets/:id/escalate`

**File:** `backend/src/routes/ticket.routes.ts`.

Insert immediately after the existing `PATCH /:id/status` handler (i.e. after line 540ish, before the TODO comment at 492–495 is replaced — see §6). Signature:

```ts
router.post(
  "/:id/escalate",
  requireAuth,
  requirePermission("tickets:escalate"),
  validateBody(escalateTicketBodySchema),
  async (req, res) => { /* … */ }
);
```

Handler steps:
1. Validate `req.params.id` is a `Types.ObjectId`; 404 if not.
2. Load `ticket = await Ticket.findById(id)`; 404 if missing.
3. Idempotency: if `ticket.status === "escalated"` and `ticket.escalatedTo?.equals(req.body.escalatedTo)`, return `200` with the current ticket (no-op) so double-clicks don't 4xx. If already escalated to a **different** target, return `409` `"Ticket is already escalated"` (the caller must reassign target via a follow-up story rather than silently overwrite).
4. Call `escalateTicket({ ticket, escalatedToUserId: new Types.ObjectId(req.body.escalatedTo), changedBy: new Types.ObjectId(req.user!.id), reason: "manual" })`.
5. Map thrown errors: `InvalidEscalationTargetError` → `400` with the error message; `InvalidStatusTransitionError` → `409` with `{ error: "Ticket cannot be escalated from its current status" }`.
6. Respond `200` with the ticket (populate `escalatedTo` name/email/role for the sidebar).

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Target is the escalator themself.** `escalateTicket` throws `InvalidEscalationTargetError`; route returns 400. Test in `ticketEscalation.service.test.ts`.
- **Target is a customer / deactivated staff / soft-deleted user.** Rejected by the role/`isActive`/`isDeleted` check in §1 → 400.
- **Target user id malformed.** Zod schema in `escalateTicketBodySchema` rejects at `validateBody` boundary → 400.
- **Ticket already escalated (same target).** Handler returns 200 no-op (idempotent — protects the sidebar's optimistic double-click).
- **Ticket already escalated (different target).** 409 — a follow-up story owns re-escalation; don't silently overwrite. Documented in the handler comment.
- **Ticket status is `"closed"`.** `ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS.closed` in §2 only allows `"in_progress"`; escalating a closed ticket throws `InvalidStatusTransitionError` → 409 `"Ticket cannot be escalated from its current status"`.
- **Notification write fails.** `createTicketNotification` / `notifyTicketOversight` are best-effort and swallow their own errors (see `backend/src/services/notification.service.ts:16-18` and `:45-47`); escalation must still return 200 and the DB state must be committed. Confirmed by reading the existing helpers.
- **Concurrent escalation.** Two agents click "Escalate" nearly simultaneously. Both load the ticket at `status: "in_progress"`, both call the service. The second will still succeed because the second `save()` overwrites `escalatedTo` — mitigate by re-fetching the ticket inside the handler *inside* a check-then-set: after `Ticket.findById(id)`, re-check `ticket.status !== "escalated"` before calling `escalateTicket`. Not a full lock, acceptable per the "best effort side effect" convention already used in this route file.
- **Story 54 (in-app notifications) not built yet.** The intake notes this fallback. In this codebase Story 54 **is** built (see `createTicketNotification` at `backend/src/services/notification.service.ts:9`), so no email fallback is required. Confirm at implementation time; if the helper is somehow missing, fall back to `sendEmail` from `backend/src/services/email.service.ts` with a "You've been escalated a ticket" template mirroring the assignment email pattern in `ticket.routes.ts` around lines 195–200.
- **`escalatedTo` populate on the list handler adds cost.** The list already populates `assignedAgent`; add `escalatedTo` to the same populate call — one extra join key, same collection.
- **Bilingual RTL layout.** The "⚠" glyph must render on the leading edge; use CSS logical properties (`margin-inline-end`) rather than `margin-right` in the button.

## Migration / Rollback

- **No DB migration.** `escalatedTo` and `statusHistory` fields already exist on `Ticket`; nothing to backfill.
- **Permission rollout:** Existing agent accounts don't automatically receive `"tickets:escalate"` (the same behaviour called out in the `customers:manage` comment at `backend/src/constants/permissions.ts:94-97`). Document in the plan's ship notes that admins must grant `"tickets:escalate"` to existing agent accounts via the staff-account editor, or the button will render disabled. No backfill script is required for this story; if desired, a one-off script mirroring `backend/scripts/backfill-chat-permission.ts` can be added.
- **Rollback:** revert the four commits (constants, service, route, frontend) — no data change to undo. If a ticket has already been escalated in production and the code is rolled back, the record retains `status: "escalated"` and `escalatedTo`; `PATCH /:id/status` still refuses `"escalated"` as a target, so those tickets can still be moved to `"in_progress"` or `"closed"` via the existing transition table extension — leave the transition rows in §2 even on partial rollback, otherwise those tickets become stuck.
